Usage: postman collection run <collectionId/Path>  [options]

Initiate a Postman collection run from a given ID or path.

Options:
  -e, --environment <path>              Specify an Id or path to a Postman
                                        Environment
  -g, --globals <path>                  Specify an Id or path to a file
                                        containing Postman Globals
     --output <folder>                  Write a YAML-based run report to the
                                        given folder. Creates a paired
                                        `<prefix>.collection-run-summary.yaml`
                                        (refreshed during the run) and
                                        streaming
                                        `<prefix>.collection-run-executions.yaml`,
                                        where prefix defaults to
                                        `<collection-slug>-<timestamp>`.
                                        Gotcha: --output streams run data to
                                        file, which keeps large runs from
                                        buffering an entire report in memory.
  -n, --iteration-count <n>             Define the number of iterations to run
  -d, --iteration-data <path>           Specify a data file to use for
                                        iterations (either JSON or CSV)
  --iteration-data-dataset <pathOrId>   Path to a .dataset.yaml (local
                                        collection) or a cloud dataset id
                                        (cloud collection) whose view drives
                                        the iteration data. Mutually exclusive
                                        with --iteration-data. Requires
                                        --iteration-data-view.
  --iteration-data-view <nameOrId>      Name or id of the view to execute
                                        (within --iteration-data-dataset). The
                                        view's result set drives one iteration
                                        per row.
  --dataset <pathOrDir>                 Pass --dataset multiple times to load
                                        several .dataset.yaml files (or
                                        directories containing them). Each is
                                        made available to collection scripts
                                        and local mock handlers as
                                        pm.datasets(<id>). When provided,
                                        auto-discovery of .dataset.yaml files
                                        from the collection's parent repo is
                                        disabled. For a cloud collection,
                                        scripts address cloud datasets by id
                                        via pm.datasets(<id>) (resolved from
                                        your `postman login` session).
                                        SECURITY: for a cloud collection this
                                        does NOT scope access — a script can
                                        pm.datasets(<anyId>) for any dataset
                                        your session can read. Only run
                                        collections you trust against a
                                        logged-in cloud session. (default: [])
  -i <id>                               Specify the request/folder id, name, or
                                        path to run from the collection. Use a
                                        path (e.g. "FolderName/RequestName") to
                                        disambiguate items with the same name.
                                        Can be specified multiple times to run
                                        multiple items (default: [])
  --global-var <value>                  Allows the specification of global
                                        variables via the command line, in a
                                        key=value format
  --env-var <value>                     Allows the specification of environment
                                        variables via the command line, in a
                                        key=value format (default: [])
  --integration-id <integration-id>     Specify the integration id for the
                                        report. (Only supported in the US
                                        region)
  --postman-api-key <apiKey>            API Key used to load the resources from
                                        the Postman API (Only supported in the
                                        US region, use 'postman login --region'
                                        to authenticate instead)
  --alias <alias>                       Specify the alias of the API key to
                                        fetch remote resources using
                                        it.[33m[39m
                                        [33m(This option is discontinued and
                                        will be removed in a future
                                        release.)[39m
  --bail [modifiers]                    Specify whether or not to gracefully
                                        stop a collection run on encountering
                                        an error and whether to end the run
                                        with an error based on the optional
                                        modifier
  --ignore-redirects                    Prevents Postman CLI from automatically
                                        following 3XX redirect responses
  -x , --suppress-exit-code             Specify whether or not to override the
                                        default exit code for the current run
  --silent                              Prevents Postman CLI from showing
                                        output to CLI
  --disable-unicode                     Forces Unicode compliant symbols to be
                                        replaced by their plain text
                                        equivalents
  --delay-request [n]                   Specify the extent of delay between
                                        requests (milliseconds) (default: 0)
  --timeout [n]                         Specify a timeout for collection run
                                        (milliseconds) (default: 0)
  --timeout-request [n]                 Specify a timeout for requests
                                        (milliseconds) (default: 0)
  --timeout-script [n]                  Specify a timeout for scripts
                                        (milliseconds) (default: 0)
  --working-dir <path>                  Specify the path to the working
                                        directory
  --no-insecure-file-read               Prevents reading the files situated
                                        outside of the working directory
  -k, --insecure                        Disables SSL validations
  --ssl-client-cert-list <path>         Specify the path to a client
                                        certificates configurations (JSON)
  --ssl-client-cert <path>              Specify the path to a client
                                        certificate (PEM)
  --ssl-client-key <path>               Specify the path to a client
                                        certificate private key
  --ssl-client-passphrase <passphrase>  Specify the client certificate
                                        passphrase (for protected key)
  --ssl-extra-ca-certs <path>           Specify additionally trusted CA
                                        certificates (PEM)
  --cookie-jar <path>                   Specify the path to a custom cookie jar
                                        (serialized tough-cookie JSON)
  --export-cookie-jar <path>            Exports the cookie jar to a file after
                                        completing the run
  --verbose                             Show detailed information of collection
                                        run and each request sent
  --mock <pathOrId>                     Start a mock server for the run, its
                                        path if it lives in your repository
                                        (relative or absolute, e.g.
                                        ./postman/mocks/orders) or its id if it
                                        lives in Postman cloud (fetched then
                                        run locally). An id needs `postman
                                        login` (or --postman-api-key).
  --port <port>                         Port for the --mock server (e.g. 4010),
                                        or "auto" for a free one. Defaults to
                                        the mock's configured port. Only valid
                                        with --mock.
  --use-mock <mapping>                  Redirect requests for a URL or
                                        {{variable}} to a mock during the run.
                                        Format: "<url>
                                        mock|mock-server:<path|id> [scenario]".
                                        Repeat the flag to redirect several
                                        URLs (one --use-mock each). Use
                                        "mock:<path>" for a mock in your
                                        repository (path relative or absolute,
                                        e.g. ./postman/mocks/orders),
                                        "mock:<id>" for a mock in Postman cloud
                                        (fetched then run locally), or
                                        "mock-server:<id>" to send requests to
                                        a deployed mock server. An id needs
                                        `postman login` (or --postman-api-key).
                                        The optional third field picks a
                                        scenario (defaults to "default").
                                        (default: [])
  --simulate <path>                     Start mock servers with fault-injection
                                        scenarios from a .sim.yaml file
  --simulation <id>                     Simulation id to record start history
                                        against when using --simulate.
  --simulate-workspace <id>             Workspace that owns the --simulate run,
                                        for recording its start history.
  --no-simulate-history                 Do not record the --simulate run in the
                                        simulation's start history.
  --report-events                       Upload results for git-native v3
                                        collection runs. Analytics are sent by
                                        default
  --no-report-events                    Do not send analytics to Postman
  -h, --help                            display help for command
Eg. postman collection run 123456-45159473-1e45-1f34-5678-1234567890ab
    postman collection run <id> --mock ./postman/mocks/orders   # a mock in your repository
    postman collection run <id> --mock 12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef  # a mock in Postman cloud
    postman collection run <id> --use-mock "{{baseurl}} mock:./mock/config.yaml delay"
    postman collection run <id> --use-mock "{{baseurl}} mock:./a.yaml" --use-mock "api.com mock-server:9d8e7f6a"
